key_insight: E-RLBM independently relaxes nonhydrodynamic modes, continuously bridging BGK and regularized collision operators without changing the Navier–Stokes viscosity.
engineering_relevance: The two-rate operator offers a low-cost way to improve lattice Boltzmann stability without implementing a full multiple-relaxation-time basis.
method: Separate the second-order hydrodynamic Hermite sector from the complementary kinetic subspace.
Assign a separate relaxation time to the kinetic subspace.
Use Chapman–Enskog analysis and flow benchmarks to assess accuracy and stability.
evidence_signal: Stability maps show enlarged stable domains; Taylor–Green tests show second-order convergence with E-RLBM error about 6% above BGK and 40% below RLBM, while a Re = 80000 double shear layer follows RLBM convergence.
watch_item: Kinetic relaxation changes direction-dependent fourth-order errors, so improved stability does not guarantee improved accuracy.
